description: The success notice 'All API keys for walker-c-job have been revoked.' is placed in the page header. When the owner revokes an agent lower in the list the header is scrolled out of view (measured top -461px), so the only visible confirmation is a small badge change from '1 ACTIVE KEY' to '0 ACTIVE KEYS'. For a security action ('cut off ci-job immediately') the owner should see an explicit confirmation.
expected: Visible confirmation next to the row or a toast fixed in the viewport.
actual: Notice off-screen; row shows 0 ACTIVE KEYS (step-3-revoked.png).
suggested_fix: Render notices in a fixed toast region, or scroll the notice into view.

description: Every row's button is named only 'Revoke access' (and 'Revoke' on the API keys tab), so assistive technology and test selectors cannot tell which agent or key a button applies to. The confirmation is a native window.confirm.
expected: aria-label 'Revoke access for walker-c-job' (and 'Revoke key walker-c-job-key').
suggested_fix: Add aria-label with the agent or key name; consider an in-app confirm dialog that names the keys and drives affected.

description: Switching tabs keeps the scroll position of the previous tab. After revoking at the bottom of Agents, the API keys tab opened scrolled to its bottom with the header, count and top of the list out of view.
expected: A new tab starts at the top.
suggested_fix: Scroll the console main region to top when the tab changes.

description: After all keys are revoked the agent row keeps an enabled 'Revoke access' button and, with 0 active keys, nothing else (no 'Remove agent', no history, no explanation of what the agent can still decrypt). A revoked agent never leaves the list.
expected: Disabled or replaced action once the agent has no active keys; an indication of status.
actual: Button still enabled (DOM check earlier in STORY-056).
suggested_fix: Show a 'Revoked' badge in place of the button.

description: The API keys list shows revoked and active keys interleaved, and each row has an unlabelled third line (the drive name) that looks like a duplicate of the agent. The story's concern about a leaked drive key has no console path: nothing says that revoking an API key does not remove the drive key from a leaked copy.
expected: Sort active first or filter; label the drive line; add a one-line note near Revoke that drive keys are separate.
suggested_fix: Add 'Drive: ' prefix; add note to the confirm text.
